description: This is not a lie: Bill Clinton once wrote Leo Casino a letter that said "Your new CD is really smokin'." That's because for the past 30 years Casino has dedicated his life to music, particularly the saxophone. He has mastered the alto, soprano, and tenor, caught a Grammy nomination, toured with Bob Marley, Peter Tosh, James Brown, and Wilson Pickett. And those are just a few luminaries who've recognized his talent. The Pittsburgh native began playing at the age of 9. He attended Howard University in Washington DC and studied under Quincy Jones. Then he moved to Miami, and the world has been better ever since. Oh, we forgot to mention he has also played with Jimi Hendrix. So what brings him to Little Hoolie's every Tuesday night. We don't know yet, but we're damn sure gonna find out.
name: Blues Night With Leo Casino

description: What's got six strings, 4 hands, a kit full of skins, and a fuzz box? The Deaf Poets, a two man band from the MIA featuring guitarist/songwriter Sean Wouters and drummer Nicolas Espinosa. Their ear friendly garage sound recalls new era White Stripes style lo-fi wildness, classic Southern riffing like the Allman Bros, some Neil Young style high notes out the vox, and a fresh coat of radio friendly, studio produced, modern prog rock. But at its heart, the music is just good old rock and roll. And maybe that's why the community has responded so positively to the group, who have over 2,300 likes on Facebook. Let the heat soak your soul for this weekly Tuesday night rocker party.
name: Deaf Poets, Heartline Fits - Rebel Run Tuesday

description: South Beach has more DJs than you can throw a laptop at. But when it comes to veterans, ones who are still spinning, there is one name that must be mentioned. Ron Luna has been working the clubs of American nightlife's greatest capital for over a decade. From residencies at bygone clubs like Honey, Bash, and Rumi, to current hot spots like Mansion, Luna continues to blaze trail of moving bodies across the great Dade County. Luna has held down Mansion's International Wednesdays for over 6 years, a lifetime in weekly party anniversaries. His popular mix of house, 80s, and hip hop continues to keep the dance floor booming, and Konflikt brings his flavor to the tables as well.
name: DJs Ron Luna and Konflikt - International Wednesdays

description: It's Cinco De Mayo, and you're not Mexican, but you love to get drunk. Right? Well, the Road understands. Take your ass down to the edge of the Miami River and soak your liver in the Independence baby! This party's got all the best food trucks, a killer DJ, the biggest parking lot this side of Nogales, and more beer than you can throw a barrel of drunken gringos at. Later, you'll see them onstage when the Los Perros Mojado Mariachi Gringo Band performs their greatest hits. So, sing along when they do their one tequila, two tequila, three tequila floor routine, then get back up, eat some tacos, grab a beer, howl at the moon, and enjoy your independence.
name: Cinco De Drinko Hot Peppa' Palooza

description: Cocowalk is one of the original outdoor mall concepts in Miami. Tourists love it, so do locals, and mariachis do too. That's where you'll find a roaming band of festivaleros crooning to your girlfriend, making you do the hat dance, and inciting more awe and wonder from your kids than you ever have. Hey, those giant guitars, cowboy boots, and awesome suits are pretty damn impressive. Tonight, the mariachis will be out in full force helping us celebrate Mexican independence day by working while we drink and have a good time. All ironies aside, between the music, our beautiful scenery, the beautiful ladies, and everybody's smiles, it's going to be an awesome night.
name: Mariachi Nomads

description: When it comes to booking the most cutting edge, underground electronic performers from around the world, the Electric Pickle is Miami's go to club. We've seen more European throwdowns there than at a Judo match in England. So it's no surprise that Tony Rohr is on the bill. The midwest born and bred DJ, producer, and live PA'er really came in to his own in Brooklyn. From there he went on to blaze a path of electronic multifacetedness across the globe, and has become a well known, constantly working, and very sought after entity. Point is, the guy is in demand for a reason, and if you enjoy experiencing a great display of dance floor talent than tonight, the Pickle is the place to be.
name: Link Presents Tony Rohr

description: What can we possibly say about The SpamAllstars that hasn't already been said? They are undeniably one of the longest running, hardest working, constantly performing, originators in the new Miami fusion sound. They definitely hold it down for the 305 and have caused more hip shaking than an earthquake at an old-folks home. They swing brass harder than a southside goon with knuckle dusters. They've got more grooves than a crate full of vinyl lp's. They've got a better live show than 30 years worth of Johnny Carson. They bring more bass than twin bazookas in a Donk Chevy. They have more presence than Christmas. They're just awesome, and that's saying something.
name: Spam AllStars

description: It's Saturday night, The Marlins just smacked the hell out of the Nationals, and now you need autotune, and lot's of it. Luckily Teddy Paine is in the building, his Cash Money buddy Jay Sean is there too, and together they will provide more electronically manipulated vocals than any most stadiums can handle. Fortunately Sun Life's state of the art sound system and your Miami bred ear drums are strong enough to digest the audials, process them, and perceive them as music. In no time at all you'll be dancing your way down from the nosebleeds to the field in a rhythmic human mass of bobbing heads, shaking booties, and cell phones lighting up the night sky.
name: T-Pain and Jay Sean - Marlins Super Saturdays

description: Desyn Masiello is a UK dude with a background as a 9-5 "computer techie." Well, one day he got sick of that gig, ditched it, and threw his total self into becoming an international DJ icon. So far, the gamble has paid off and he has had incredible success in getting gigs, creating albums, and making a name for himself around the world. One of his specialties is re-editing classic tracks for a dance floor interpretation. The Beatles don't necessarily represent club music, but in Masiello's hands they come off as big room bangers. It is his talent for giving the people what they want, as filtered through his own unique sensibility for excellent craft work that makes him the star he is.
name: Desyn Masiello

description: He may be an English DJ and producer, but he's also a Miami businessman. As co-owner of The Vagabond, Digweed stakes a major claim on Miami nightlife, and especially the downtown party scene. But he's also a major force in the world of entertainment. The high end, bottle guzzling clientele that frequent joints like SET love him just as much as the hipsters across the bridge. And so it is that tonight, alongside Louis Dee, Digweed throws down a set that will have the models strutting, the ballers filling tables, and the tourists awed at the spectacle of South Beach. With a career that spans into last century, we can be sure he's got the experience to keep the party moving all night long, and morning too.
name: John Digweed

description: Miami loves John Digweed. And we are pretty sure the feeling is mutual. Proof: Just this past Miami Music Week, he headlined at Cameo, the annual Sunset Cruise, and the Vagabond — the 14th Street nightclub he co-owns. But even after March's full serving of the Magic City, the British legend is back for more. Set will be Digweed's playground for this Miami redux party. Often described as “a DJ's DJ,” he's a breed of superstar turntablist that existed before acts such as Tiësto, Deadmau5, and Swedish House Mafia crossed over into the mainstream. Will Digweed ever join them on the other side? Probably not, but that's a good thing. Instead of paying $200 to see this master at work, Set's admission is a bargain at $25. A tony setting and house music just might make the hung-over Monday-morning commute worth it.
name: John Digweed

description: It's been a tough week. Our old lady left us, she shacked up with our cousin, we went to confront them, but our gun was out of bullets. We got pulled over on the way there, caught a parking ticket that afternoon, and ended up with a DUI that night. When we got out of jail the bar was out of whiskey, the beer was flat, somebody stole our favorite seat, and the tender called up our tab. We got our ass kicked in an alley, woke up in a puddle in the gutter, and somebody stole our shoes. On the way home we stubbed our toe, and when we got there an eviction notice was stuck to the front door. Let's just say we've got the blues. The only thing that could possibly make us feel better right about now is listening to Big Poppa E wail on that guitar of his, and maybe an ice cold Budweiser at Tobacco Road. Let's go!
name: Big Poppa E and The E Band

description: Crust punks, they smell pretty bad. If you've ever been to a noise show, in Miami, in the Summer, then you're probably already aware of the olfactory assault. But even that doesn't compare to the level of ferocity their chosen style of music employs. It's loud, it's fast, and it's heavier than a bag full of anvils, on a boulder, on a Cadillac. That's why the 5th annual 305 Fest ought to be on your agenda for tonight. Bands from Puerto Rico to Massachusetts, and some points in between will smashfully rock your stinking jungle-rotten staph infected socks off, or your freshly laundered ones, the show's open to everybody.
name: The 5th Annual 305 Fest

description: “For the first time since I was a child, I — who normally sleep naked except for diamond earrings — am not wearing them,” Mario Cantone utters. He's reading from One Lifetime Is Not Enough, Zsa Zsa Gabor's memoir about her 72 hours in jail. It's part of Celebrity Autobiography, where stars read excerpts from other celebrity tell-alls. At past performances, Saturday Night Live's Rachel Dratch channeled Good Morning America's Joan Lunden to explain she oils doorknobs so that her early mornings don't wake her family. And actors Kristen Johnston and Ryan Reynolds read from the dueling memoirs of ex-lovers Loni Anderson and Burt Reynolds. Here's hoping all of this heavy-handed sarcasm shames future celebrities from taking their insipid lives so seriously in book form. When Celebrity Autobiography hits the Arsht Center's Carnival Studio Theater this week, there will be no shortage of material to be mocked. You might hear everything from vintage Vanna White Speaks to more current dribble, such as Britney Spears's diary. The Miami stop, which runs through May 15, includes live readings by Cantone, Dratch, Sharon Gless, Desperate Housewives' Roger Bart, and show creators Dayle Reyfel and Eugene Pack. Celebrity Autobiography won the 2009 Drama Desk Award for Unique Theatrical Experience.
name: Celebrity Autobiography

description: Comedian Reggie Watts’s real name is Reginald Lucien Frank Roger Watts, but there are hundreds more characters living inside him. And each of his personalities comes with its own instrument. Launched from Brooklyn’s alt-comedy scene, Watts’s routines are a fluid mix of accents, personas, and musical interludes. They are as disorienting as they are genius. That’s why Conan O’Brien handpicked Watts to open his recent Legally Prohibited From Being Funny on Television Tour. Well, that and his great hair. Haloed by a giant, trademark Afro, Watts beat-boxes, hums, and raps, all of which he loops via a Line 6 DL4 effects pedal. Over that, he channels a motley crew: Brits, New Jersey cabbies, effeminate Southern men, his grandfather from Cleveland, and sometimes Bill Cosby. Last year, he released his musical comedy album, Why $#!+ So Crazy? The album’s “Fuck Shit Stack” video, in which Watts satirizes hip-hop songs, went viral thanks to the comic’s stream-of-consciousness profanity laced with social commentary: “I wear bullet-proof vests for no apparent reason/Other than to create a false sense of importance.” Is this melodic man with multiple personalities the next big thing? Decide for yourself when Watts performs this Thursday and Friday at Light Box at Goldman Warehouse. Presented by the Miami Light Project.
name: Reggie Watts

description:
Way back in 1972, Grandpa Levine built a little hotel on a sleepy one-lane road in what's now Palmetto Bay. Today, the place has become a destination for comics and the crazy people who love them, all thanks to third-generation hotelier and Comedy Inn executive producer Mike Levine. Every Friday at 9:30 p.m., Levine's Comedy Inn at the Quality Inn invades the hotel's grand ballroom, dropping a gaggle of jokers onstage and packing 75 gigglers into the seats. "The ballroom is a great place for comedy," Levine says. "It's an homage to the great ballrooms of the past, like in the Catskill Mountains, albeit on a smaller scale."

So show up early, laugh late, and sleep over -- it's a freaking hotel.

Some things just go together. Peanut butter and jelly. Cookies and milk. The Captain and Tennille. And, apparently, comedy and cigars. The shows are headlined by comics from BET’s Comic View and from Comedy Central, and hosted by Miami’s own “very hairy and very sexy” Tomahawk. Local comedy connoisseurs might recognize Tomahawk from his starring roles in Six Comics from Miami and the Comedy in the Living Room series.

For those unfamiliar with his work, the films are available on Amazon.com or from the trunk of Tomahawk’s car. Recognizing a can’t-miss marketing opportunity, Chop Shop Barber Shop jumped to sponsor the evenings. “They’re the only barbershop I know that was featured in Jet magazine,” says Tomahawk. Head to Aromas of Havana at 10 p.m. (Latin Standard Time) and smoke ’em if you got ’em, or get ’em there. Tickets cost $10. Call 305-940-0988.

description:

Born Alexis Fernandez Mena, the Cuban entertainer puts the fab in fabulous daily, but you can catch him/her live and in living color each week during Cabaret Fridays at La Paloma European Steak & Lobster House. Beginning at 10:00 p.m., Marytrini and friends will have you dancing in the aisles with a night of song, comedy, and more costume changes than you can probably handle. “It’s very classy, very beautiful, with beautiful clothes. It’s hard to explain, but it’s a great show,” says La Paloma owner Maria Staub. Have a bite to eat at La Paloma and you can watch the show for free, but if you arrive after 10:00, you gotta cough up 10 bucks at the door and fulfill a two-drink requirement. Call 305-891-0505 for reservations.

description:
The infusion of Latin traditions into Miami culture requires that upon entering Miami-Dade County, you trade in the rules you used to live by for a set saturated in Goya spices. Here coladas are piping-hot and sipped for breakfast instead of on-the-rocks and guzzled by the pitcher, and when you speak of salsa, you’re usually referring to the dance, not a dip for tortilla chips. But although you’ve perfected the art of ordering a Cuban coffee sin azúcar, your dance moves are another story. And since your Hispanic friends giggle behind your back at the stiffness of your swivel, the crew at Salsa Mia will teach you how to execute the sensuous and flirtatious dance with ease – and rhythm.

Each Tuesday at Energy Fitness, two-hour salsa classes will take you through all the steps, whether you’re a beginner or a hoofing legend. New students, just show up 15 minutes before the class begins and you’ll be grooving before you know it. Classes start at $20. Call 305-987-3033 or visit salsamia.com for more information.

description: Of all of Alfred Hitchcock's films, his 1935 classic The 39 Steps would probably be the most difficult to adapt to the stage. Yet this week, Actors' Playhouse presents a theatrical adaptation of this complicated spy thriller — full of murder, secret organizations, conspiracies, and dudes in wigs — and injects it with a healthy dose of Monty Python. The movie tells the story of Richard Hannay, who takes a mysterious woman to his apartment one night. Next thing he knows, she's dead with a knife in her back and a map in her hand. Thus Hannay is thrust into one of Hitch's favorite go-to plot lines: an innocent man on the run trying to unravel a mystery. The 39 Steps, a two-time Tony Award-winning play, is filled with laughs, split-second wardrobe changes, inventive stagecraft, and a death-defying finale. For the Actors' Playhouse production, a cast of four plays all 150 characters from the movie. Catch this hilarious suspense thriller at the Miracle Theatre when the show opens this Wednesday.
name: The 39 Steps

description: No doubt, vibrators are therapeutic. We women live in a stressful world littered with selfish men. Many a woman’s most satisfying sexual partner is a battery-operated, brightly colored phallus. In fact, in the darker ages of medicine, these little stress-relievers were used by doctors as a treatment for female hysteria. Sure, getting off thanks to a doctor is something porn sites make a ton of money peddling of these days, but the full story of early vibrators reveals more about the way women have been treated by the medical profession (and men in general) than about kinkiness. Sarah Ruhl’s Pulitzer Prize- and Tony-nominated play In the Next Room (or the Vibrator Play) looks at the history of this unusual practice by examining two Victorian women’s experiences with the fun tool. Catch some onstage O’s when the play opens Saturday at 8 p.m. at GableStage. The show runs Thursday to Sunday through June 12
name: In the Next Room (or the Vibrator Play)

description: If we had known being on a reality-TV show was so profitable, we would have signed up for the first season of Survivor faster than you can say fame whore. Snooki and those Jersey Shore assholes will make about a million dollars this year, and that’s just for their fourth season. And let’s not forget about the housewives. The Real Housewives of Atlanta star Nene Leakes is ever expanding her brand. She has Celebrity Apprentice and a book deal, and now she is a thespian. No, not a lesbian (like Kim Zolciak once was); Leakes is taking a turn on the drama stage. She is starring in Theo London’s award-winning play, Loving Him Is Killing Me. Also in the cast are soul singer Angie Stone, sexy model Tyson Beckford, music legend Lenny Williams, and Joe “Tiny” Barrino from VH1’s Fantasia Barrino reality show. From what we hear, the play is “filled with endearing characters, hilarious moments, and a family who uses faith and the power of prayer to overcome the temptations.” Temptations like what? All we can hope is that Tyson takes off his shirt and Nene rips off someone’s wig. The show opens Friday at the James L. Knight Center and runs through Sunday.

description: You snooze, you lose, right? Well, not in the case of the The Red Thread, a new production opening at the kid-friendly PlayGround Theatre. When artistic director Stephanie Ansin snoozes, she creates. She wrote The Red Thread after Fernando Calzadilla, co-writer and production designer of the play, read to her while she dozed in his studio. Since then, Ansin and Calzadilla have done a lot of research, weaving into their play elements from the martial arts, philosophy, geography, mysticism, and music of China. The final product is the story of a young woman’s heroic efforts to rescue her father’s surprisingly miraculous masterpiece. The PlayGround will host New York actors Christian T. Chan, Christina Jun, and Kate Shine, who will join local actors Melissa Almaguer, Troy Davidson, Stephen Elliot Kaiser, Marjorie O’Neill-Butler, and Jesús Quintero for the production.
name: The Red Thread

description: Once upon a time, an unusual German boy named Hansel fell in love with Luther, a U.S. soldier, but East Germany’s communist shackles kept them apart. In order to flee, the two would have to marry as man and woman. So Hansel underwent surgery to take over his mother Hedwig’s identity. Unfortunately, the surgery didn’t go as planned, and Luther eventually left the malformed and heartbroken Hedwig. Now recovered from the breakup, she assembled a rock band, Hedwig and the Angry Inch, comprised of Korean-born army wives. In 1998, John Cameron Mitchell joined forces with Stephen Trask to rock the world with the musical Hedwig and the Angry Inch, the groundbreaking tale of a transgender rock singer. After an international tour and a series of awards, the story made it onto the big screen in 2001. Inviting South Florida to take part in the “Hedhead” phenomenon, Infinite Abyss Productions brings Hedwig back to life at Empire Stage this week. Promising to be “tran-tastic,” Hedwig and the Angry Inch will preview this Friday and Saturday.
name: Hedwig and the Angry Inch

description:
Downtown Miami is a work in progress. Amid the giant glass and steel structures that continue to sprout like weeds, there’s an earnest and dedicated group of culture-lovers striving to populate the oft-desolate area with fun events. The Cultural Development Group, for instance, is a nonprofit that seeks to bring Miami’s city streets to life with the sounds of music. One of its coolest projects is Miami Unsigned, a weekly musical showcase that shines a light on our great repository of local talent.

“We’re working with the mayor to put as much live music as we can in downtown Miami. We do different genres every week, and we welcome all kinds of artists,” explains founder and director Eric Shenkman. Sounds sweet to us, dude. Tonight Miami Unsigned takes over Soya y Pomodoro, and the smooth sounds of the Dereck Fairholm Trio will fill the lofty space. Stop by for a hot dose of local jazzadelic rhythms at 9:00.
name: Miami Unsigned

description:
What happened to the good ol’ days, when aspiring artists hit the streets to bombard anybody and everybody with their talents? Now it seems hopefuls are content with posting cheesy videos on YouTube or creating glitter-laden MySpace pages and praying for their “big break.” We understand these methods might work, but it couldn’t hurt to try meeting people face-to-face. Which is why we’re sending you to Hollywood -- no, not in California, the one in Broward County -- to perform in a superofficial Industry Artist Showcase. In addition to your mama, A&R reps from major record labels such as Sony, Universal, EMI, and BMG will be in the audience.

“Our mission is to get indie artists signed,” says talent coordinator and the night’s host, Chris Imperial. “We’re not just looking for musicians; we’re looking for poets, comedians, whoever. We’re looking for people that are gonna be the next big whatever.” So if you claim to be a hustla, a go-getta, and “on your grind,” call Chris at 754-214-6024 or e-mail him at grassroots3000@yahoo.com to get on the list to perform. Doors open at 8:00, and all ages are welcome, at the Legends Café, 2029 Harrison St., Hollywood. Admission is $10.
name: Industry Artist Showcase

description:
Each and every Monday for the past four years and three months, the Miami Pipeline has been a place for the be’s and the wannabes of the music business to mingle and jam. Acting as a music-loving Dr. Frankenstein, Miami legend DJ Bass and his wife, Angela Bowen, created Miami Mic Mondays -- a place where artists like Trick Daddy, Pretty Ricky, Joe Blow, and Jane Doe come to perform, learn about the music biz, and meet influential people.

“It’s not just a regular open-mike night; it’s a school type of thing,” says Bowen. “We teach them the actual business, copyrighting, press kits, how to get on Internet radio.” And after you’ve gotten schooled properly, you can sign up to show a roomful of folks your mike skills, because week after week, the audience is packed with music execs, lyrics-lovers, fellow artists, and anyone else you can imagine. Artists pay a $10 donation, but it’s free to watch. Doors open at 8:30 p.m.
name: Miami Mic Mondays

description:
Muddy Waters most famously called for someone to “bring me champagne when I'm thirsty, bring me reefer when I want to get high.” But had ol’ Muddy extended the list of intoxicants, he might have included bourbon for when he wanted to sing the blues. There’s something about the combination of Kentucky-produced, aged grain alcohol and the mournful, gritty music born from the African-American experience that goes together divinely. The folks at Bourbon Steak at the Fairmont Turnberry Isle Resort and Club have figured out that winning combination. Their new weekly Bourbon & Blues night is packing in crowds of music-loving gourmands.

Begin your evening with half-price signature cocktails and reduced-price appetizers at the bar from 6 to 8 p.m., a special social hour called Raise Your Spirits that takes place every weekday. Then from 7 to 10 p.m., a local blues band will present its spin on the sound most often associated with the Deep South, Chicago, and men such as John Lee Hooker, Lead Belly, and Robert Johnson. Through the end of this month, admired duo Albert Castiglia and Graham Drout will do their thing while dinner is served. And what a dinner it is: Musically inspired offerings include chicken and waffles, beer-battered grouper, barbeque pulled-pork sandwiches, crab beignets, and let’s not forget a 25 percent discount on the restaurant’s impressive bourbon and American whiskey selections. Order it neat, on the rocks, as a Manhattan, or sour with a maraschino cherry garnish. It always goes down smooth.
name: Bourbon & Blues

description:
It seems like every bar, restaurant, and corner store offers a happy hour. But few realize that overcooked hot wings and watered-down drinks do not a happy hour make. As a matter of fact, just thinking about that crap makes us kinda sad. But one of our favorite downtown restaurants, Soya y Pomodoro, is enticing us with a new happy hour, and this one actually paints a smile on our faces.

Its called Beat Traffic, a name that commands us to eschew rush hour in the car for rush hour at the bar, so we can bob our heads to live music on a barstool instead of rocking to canned banter in the drivers seat. Every Friday from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m., imported beers are two for five dollars, and glasses of wine are two for seven. Plus the tapas menu says nothing about baskets of Costco hot wings. Now were happy.
name: Beat Traffic

description:
It’s no secret that on South Beach, glitz rules. Even a naive tourist whose knowledge of the Magic City stems from a few episodes of Miami Ink can tell you that. But it takes a true 305 native to know where to find underground art and music. Usually it’s on the mainland in gritty downtown Miami, but there are a few crannies in SoBe where independent culture still thrives. Take, for instance, Maxine Restaurant at the Catalina Hotel. Here up-and-coming artists take the stage during Fizz Wednesdays.

This month dei7 -- featuring Derin Young, Yoel Delsol, Orlando Guanche, and Daniel Stable -- plays its brand of soul mixed with Cuban rhythms. And tonight will be the last night artist Jesus Gini’s Pop Carousel Horses collection is on display at Maxine, so be sure to catch the colorful and creative paintings of flamboyant fashions for merry-go-round mares. Take advantage of drink specials from 7:00 to 8:00. Music performances take place at 7:00 and 9:00.

description:
It’s Saturday night and your stomach is growling, hungry for some culinary comfort. So you head to The Mahogany Grille for some soul food, and find yourself indulging in Asiago cheese grits, bread pudding, fried chicken, and waffles. Your belly is full, but you’re still feeling an emptiness deep inside. There’s an old saying that declares music is like food for your soul, and tonight you don’t have to move far from the dinner table to feed that little bugger. Every Friday and Saturday night from 9:00 to midnight, the intimate lounge next to the restaurant pulses with live jazz that’ll have you moving and grooving and feeling like you’re at the Cotton Club.

The swaying of your hips will let you work off that meal, but even if you don’t plan on grabbing a bite to eat, we’re sure you’ll enjoy the fantastic aromas just the same.
name: Live Jazz at The Mahogany Grille

description:
If a group of dudes poked their heads through the door tonight at Uva Lounge, they might think they had entered the ultimate straight mans fantasy. The weekly Sunday-night bash, Ambiance at Uva, is all about sexy ladies getting to know each other and hot dancers shimmying on tabletops. But this party is intended to give Miami lesbians what theyve been looking for -- a hot event away from the tired South Beach scene.

Besides the go-go dancers and the hot tracks laid down by DJ V Butterfly and DJ Kiki, the bash features drag king shows and a full menu of delicious food served until the wee hours. And tonight a live performance by God-Des and She, a band that made hearts flutter when it appeared on Showtimes The L Word, will leave the ladies screaming for more. Admission for tonights special event is $20; VIP admission is $150. Call 786-521-1777.

description: The puff paint on his Christian Audigier hat glistens under the sexy lighting at Red Room, and the crowd is transfixed by his drunken confidence. His boyish grin suggests he might sing a little Enrique, but his spiky hair disagrees and makes the crowd think he’ll choose ’N Sync. Yeah, definitely ’N Sync. He licks his lips, ready to give onlookers the show that his bathroom mirror is sick of watching, and then: “All right — stop, collaborate, and listen. Ice is back with my brand-new invention.” It’s karaoke hell for the sober, but if it’s done right, you’ll be singing along before Mr. Spikyhair Ice gets to the chorus. SoBe’s newest place for live, amateur crooning is Beauty and the Beats, TAI Entertainment’s partnership with Michael Madd and the latest nightlife offering trying to pry you away from yet another Law & Order marathon. Each Sunday beginning at 10 p.m., beautiful people will converge upon the mike, and a few pros will swing through to show us how it’s done. It’s a secret as to who will actually show up, but we’ll trust Tommy Pooch’s, Michael Madd’s, and Alan Roth’s Rolodexes if you will. Call 786-276-6772 or email skybarreservations@morganshotelgroup.com for table reservations.
name: Beauty and the Beats

description:
For the past couple of months, your Mondays have been moody, miserable, and muddled. More than once you've wondered, Where have my sexy vibes and happy feelings gone? You've even found yourself in the midtown area, looking for the cool kids who used to run to the District for a reprieve from the week that had only just begun. Now you can wipe that malcontented look from your face and sport the peaceful Mona Lisa smile again, because Mello Mondays are back to save you from the blues.

The groove of this spoken-word dinner party has moved a little farther north, to Bluster, but other than the locale, everything else has remained the same. It's still the best spot to vibe with an eclectic crowd while the rhythms of hip-hop and the lyricism of poetry float around you; there's still better-than-bar food for you to nosh on, and you'll still wash away the madness and end up feeling Mello. HBO Def Poet Asia will host, and local and national artists will hit the stage all night — politically conscious rappers Dead Prez just rocked the mike for the grand opening. Tickets start at ten bucks before 10 p.m. Doors open at 8.
name: Mello Mondays

description: Us saguesera kids usually get left out of all the cool, hip cultural events going on in Miami due to our geographical disability (not living on the East Side). Lucky for us, with the Bird Road Arts District making a comeback and events like the Hell Yeah Open Mic, it looks like we can start saving some gas money and get culture closer to home. Speak! Fridays at Inner Look provides a platform for expression to artists, musicians, spoken word artists, dancers, and actors. This place is so hot that spoken word artists from HBO Def Poetry and Brave New Voices regularly grace the stage.
name: Speak! Fridays

description:
Most people associate open-mike poetry nights with tie-dye, sneaky hits from Pyrex bowls, crusty flip-flops, and the stink of patchouli. But the Bohemia Room at Vlada Lounge is the “Boom Boom Pow” version of those hippie nightmares. Sure, there’ll be some political ranting, but it’ll likely be followed by Marvin Gaye’s “Mercy Mercy Me.” Resident DJ and house poet Anomaly chooses tracks according to the tone of the poet’s work onstage.

Host Ingrid B describes the Bohemia Room’s audience as sophisticated, college-educated, single urbanites in their mid-20s to mid-30s who are “grown and sexy.” The self-described “raunchy and hilarious” host offers the evening as something different from the regular weeknight. Every Wednesday evening, you can listen to poets pontificate about everything from sex to health care, down a few drinks, and meet some financially stable and intellectually stimulating hotties.
name: The Bohemia Room

Well tonight they bring that mayhem to the oldest punk rock bar in all of Miami, (Ok, it's the only punk rock bar in all of Miami, and Churchill's will open her beer and whiskey soaked arms to the band and welcome them onto her stage. The band has been perfecting their chops since 2008 and now they are ready to smash their music through your skull and make you understand.

description: Women are rejoicing from Hialeah to Homestead. Why? Because Aqua Girl is back, which means that at party after party of lesbian, bisexual, and trans women will celebrate their right to make out with each other. And believe us, there will be plenty of making out. Aqua Girl, which runs through Saturday, starts off with Thursday’s Traffic Jam kick-off dance party at Dream Nightclub . On Friday from 11 a.m. until 5 p.m., listen to the sounds of DJ Citizen Jane and DJ G-Spot at the Surfcomber Resort (1717 Collins Ave., Miami Beach), while Sapphic swimming ensues at the Splash Pool Party. Tickets cost $9 to $17. Take the celebration (and your outfit) up a notch by enjoying Dish, Aqua Girl’s culinary affair at Smith & Wollensky (1 Washington Ave., Miami Beach) Saturday from 8 to 10 p.m. Tickets cost $50 to $60. Then round out all of your presummer lovin’ with Afterglow, Aqua Girl’s official closing party at Score Nightclub (727 Lincoln Rd., Miami Beach), featuring DJ Zehno, DJ Kaprah, and Lady M on the turntables from 9 p.m. until 2 a.m. Event passes cost $108 to $319.

Welcome to logic 9.0 motherfucker. We got it on lock. Good thing there will be enough bass produced tonight to rattle aliens out of their UFO's all the way in the Canada's of outer space. Truth from New Zealand headlines and a hurricane of local talent supports when Dub Step takes over 14th street. Flood your brain with wobbles and snaps, torque your body till reality floats off, lean back, and have a good timer.

description: DJ Skribble may be Italian-American, but that didn't stop him from spinning in a group called Young Black Teenagers in the early 90s. From there he went on to work on Wyclef's first album, to releasing MDMA, Essential Dance 2000 on Atlantic Records. You may also know him for teaming up with MTV on Total Request Live, The Grind, and other tv shows. He's also responsible for a 24 count discography of albums, compilations, and singles and at least 35 remixes. Hey, he's a busy guy, and that means he's on the road for 200 shows a year. He started out in 1980, was the first DJ to have hos own toy and video game, and also performs regularly with guitar dude Dave Navarro. Basically, go to the damn show.
name: DJ Skribble

description: Miami in the 1970s offered a golden era of high school rock bands. Mantrap was one of many, but in their time, one of the best to play what were called Open House dances, weekly, low budget parties for the youth where hundreds would gather and crowd halls from The Grove to Hialeah. Mantrap bega in 1974, and disbanded in 1980. But their fans never forgot the good times, and in 2009 the group got back together for a one-off gig. It was such a success that El Conjunto Universal, the kings of the Cuban Bailes (weekly parties going on at the same time as the Open Houses), decided to get back together for a reunion show as well. This was also a great success. Now, for the first time in over 30 years, the two bands are joining forces for a party of such epic proportions you'll be screaming "Encore! till the year 2040.
name: Conjunto Universal and Mantrap (Live)

description: Quick geography lesson: Where is Suriname located? The former Dutch colony is actually just a plane ride from Miami and perhaps the last place you’d expect as the home turf of an emerging DJ. But South America’s smallest country bore Chuckie, the latest sensation behind the turntables. Calling the Netherlands home these days, Clyde Narain has quickly climbed to the top of the house music scene thanks to tight production skills and remixes. (Let’s face it, remixing for the likes of David Guetta and Bob Sinclar gets you noticed.) But perhaps Chuckie’s biggest accomplishment is his Dirty Dutch parties, a series of events happening all over the world and the reason he is booked at LIV for the rest of the year, including this Saturday. Along with Miami-by-way-of-Morocco DJ Mednas, Chuckie will take over the Fontainebleau megaclub and give you good reason to pop bottle after bottle of overpriced champagne.
name: Chuckie

description: Quick geography lesson: Where is Suriname located? The former Dutch colony is actually just a plane ride from Miami and perhaps the last place you’d expect as the home turf of an emerging DJ. But South America’s smallest country bore Chuckie, the latest sensation behind the turntables. Calling the Netherlands home these days, Clyde Narain has quickly climbed to the top of the house music scene thanks to tight production skills and remixes. (Let’s face it, remixing for the likes of David Guetta and Bob Sinclar gets you noticed.) But perhaps Chuckie’s biggest accomplishment is his Dirty Dutch parties, a series of events happening all over the world and the reason he is booked at LIV for the rest of the year, including this Saturday. Along with Miami-by-way-of-Morocco DJ Mednas, Chuckie will take over the Fontainebleau megaclub and give you good reason to pop bottle after bottle of overpriced champagne.
name: Chuckie

description: Between Mixed Culture and Jahfe, there's enough Caribbeanism to send the night into a tropical inspired musical experience that can only be had in Miami, where Trenchtown meets South Beach. These two bands explore the heritage of sounds from countries like Jamaica, Haiti, Brazil, and Puerto Rico. They make unlimited world music with an easy skankin' tempo that sets your body moving as if by reflex. Everything you've heard about Jazid being amazing is true. For a club that has survived as long where it has doing what it does it has to be. The music doesn't dissappoint, the atmosphere is remarkable, the people watching is top notch, and again, the music is awesome.
name: Mixed Culture and Jahfe

description: Across the street from Maurice Gibb Memorial Park, this long running local's bar is a late night institution for dancing, drinks, and ladies. On Monday nights, if you want reggae, dis be de place. Jean Pokito is the bandleader for Jean P. Jam, a world beat rockin' band playing "deep roots" music. Jean P. has toured Europe, Asia, and the USA playing with other top bands, and his own group is busy all over tri-county playing private parties, corporate functions, and special events. His Monday residency at Purdy is where he gets into sets of jams that keep the drinks pouring and the people dancing until five o'clock in the morning.
name: Jean P. Jam - Monday Night Reggae

description:
Spearheading much of mainland Miami nightlife's response to the tragedy in Haiti is a man known as the Haitian Hillbilly. Born Alain Maximilien, this hipster redneck (of sorts) not only spent many of his more formative years on the island nation, but also his father runs Maison des Anges, a 120-child orphanage just outside Port-au-Prince. And while (thankfully) everyone there survived the quake, the structure itself did not fare as well. Both children and staff are all living in tents set up on the orphanage's grounds.

That's the good news. The bad news is that Maximilien lost a half-brother.

But, as you might suspect, this is not Maximilien's first rodeo in that perennially crippled nation. He has been involved periodically with (and remains a staunch advocate of) Project Medishare, a University of Miami School of Medicine group that has brought health care to the Haitian hinterlands since 1994. And his persona was actually born in that country, after a chat in a Port-au-Prince bar led to a spot on Radio NBC. To read the full piece about the Haitian Hillbilly on Crossfade, click here.
name: The Haitian Hillbilly

description: The demise of Bella Rose seems to have given Kill Your Idol exclusive property rights to a certain slice of South Beach. With almost zero competition, the bar has latched onto the area’s street scene. In a space that was once home to house-head fave Blue and then the abomination known as Vince Neil’s Feelgood’s, this party spot has morphed into hipsterati central. In a certain way, Kill Your Idol is the Beach’s version of NE 14th Street’s Bar, a dark and semiprivate playground where the cool kids hang. But this place isn’t trying to mimic downtown grit. It already has more authenticity than it needs, and Tuesday’s Rumble party is definitive proof. Every week, DJ Haitian Hillbilly lures some of the best local acts onstage while you drown yourself in $5 pints of PBR and shots of Jack Daniel’s or Southern Comfort. Choose your drinks wisely, though — your too-cool-for-school rep depends on it.
name: Rumble

description: During club nights at chichi South Beach venues, ladies wear dresses that resemble sausage casings, fellas don bedazzled T-shirts, and everyone waits outside, hoping to be one of the chosen few. This seems even more ridiculous during summer than the rest of the year. Who wants to stand behind a velvet rope for hours while trying to get the attention of a holier-than-thou bouncer when its 1,000 degrees outside? All hail the no-fuss, no-muss clubs that keep the AC high and the bullshit low. On Tuesdays, your laidback lick is at Buck15's Takeout Tuesdays, where DJ Keen One plays sound selector and you chug cheap cocktails. Located above the yummy Miss Yip Chinese Café, the spot is hard to find. But just follow the kid in the lime green skinny jeans — he'll know the way. The party kicks off at 10 p.m. and rolls until that wonderful time of "until."
name: Takeout Tuesdays

description:
They have the power to save lives, so it's only right that not just anyone can slap on a pair of headphones and call himself a DJ. They scratch vinyl in ways that make party people fall in love, so although skipping through your iPod might make you feel like a sound selector, alas, you're not. But this is America, and there's a class for learning how to be any type of awesome you desire.

To become the next DJ Immortal, Self Born, Rob Riggs, Hurricane, or Bounce, sign up for the new-year term at Scratch DJ Academy. In fact, you can mix and chicka-chicka on the turntables right next to those guys if you're up for the challenge. As part of Class Room 423, every Wednesday at Love Hate Lounge (423 Washington Ave., Miami Beach), lucky students will be able to play an actual (nonpaying) gig, carry the crates, rock the crowd, and look dope while doing it. So sign up for a class, from beginner to advanced, in mixing and scratching or even beatmaking, to get your turn in the spotlight.
name: Scratch DJ Academy

description: Some shows on the boob tube will suck you dry, leaving your brain with no sign of function or creativity. Others are so good they make you want to quit your job and be a full-time resident of your living room couch. Mad Men is one of the latter. This AMC program (way too awesome to be called a simple "show") has inspired a resurgence of '60s fashion and culture. Hopefully, it's also made a few corporations rethink their policies on in-office smoking and drinking. Of course, the crazy kids of Mad Men work at a fictional ad agency, and you, well, you work somewhere real and it's probably not as cool as Sterling Cooper. But once a week at the Mayfair Hotel's Lobby Bar, you can sure act like it is. Mad Men Mondays takes on the spirit of your favorite televised guilty pleasure in the forms of Rob Roys, Tom Collinses, and Harvey Wallbangers, which all go for $3.50 from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. The mood will be set by the music of the time (and modern retakes), Mad Men episodes on the big screen, and you doing the funky watusi.
name: Mad Men Mondays

description:
There are those lucky few born for the loftiest pursuits, such as the office of the president of the United States of America. Then there are others, even luckier, who were put on Earth to get their wee-wees and vajayjays wet in exchange for cash money. The rest of us just watch.

Now, if you're a future statesman, stay home and save your reputation. But if you belong to the wee-wee and vajayjay wetters, get lubed this Tuesday at Dream, when Porn to Be a Star drops its pants. Kicking off at 10 p.m., the whole thing's being described as a "fucking house party," but it's uncertain whether that's literal. So show up fully clothed and then go with the flow as DJs Dissmiss, Hugo M, and Icecold dish out the "foreplay" and Ron Luna drops "orgas-mix." As for the rest of us, we'll be there too. You know, just watching. Admission is free for women, and men pay a $20 cover.
name: Porn to Be a Star

description:
Remember when indie dance parties were low-key affairs with cheap drinks, a lax door policy, and great music? Luckily for us, there are people looking to bring that back. Back in the day, Nightdrive started at the News Lounge but never seemed to gain the popularity it deserved. It was a Thursday-night party with no frills, great local DJs, and decent drink specials. But at some point, the bash seemed to run out of gas.
Or so we thought. For the last few months, party dudes Patrick and Moshe have been bringing the Tuesday tunes to Bar and all the beauties who hang there. Nightdrive lives!
name: Nightdrive

description: Get two-for-one drinks while the ladies dance.
name: Happy Hour

description:
Tuesday nights are so boring. There’s nothing good on television now that Law & Order: SVU switched days, and the weekend still seems so far away. Luckily for you, there’s always a magical place called Planeta Macho.

Score hosts what has become the premier Latin gay night in Miami. Every Tuesday night, Ricardito La La and his Hot Dancers — really, that’s what they’re called — help get the crowd pumped for the salsa, reggaeton, merengue, and whatever else your weary Hispanic heart desires. It’s all brought to you by DJs George Ferrero and Javier Sainz. But don’t think South Beach’s largest gay club stops there. Planeta Macho also boasts performances by Miami’s Favorite Divas, and those sexy ladies are bound to give you the energy to power you through the rest of the week. To get on the list, call 305-535-1111.
name: Planeta Macho

description: Get two-for-one drinks all evening.
name: Happy Hour

Born Alain Maximilien, this hipster redneck (of sorts) not only spent many of his more formative years in the island nation; his father runs Maison des Anges, a 120-child orphanage just outside Port au Prince. And while (thankfully) everyone on site survived the quake, the structure itself did not fare as well. Both children and staff are all living in tents set up on the orphanage's grounds.

That's the good news. The bad news is that Maximilien lost a half-brother.

But, as you might suspect, this is not Maximilien's first rodeo in that perennially crippled nation. He's periodically been involved with (and remains a staunch advocate of) Project Medishare, a University of Miami School of Medicine group that has been bringing healthcare to the Haitian hinterlands since 1994. And his persona was actually born in that country, after a chat in a Port-au-Prince bar led to a spot on Radio NBC. To read the full piece on the Haitian Hillbilly on Crossfade, click here.
name: The Haitian Hillbilly

description: Get $100 call bottles and a $75 champagne room.
name: Call It Champagne

description:
​New Times recently gave Kill Your Idol, the new bar occupying the old Blue space, the nod for Best Jukebox. It's true -- the venue is part of the extended Vagabond / Lost Weekend / Respectable Street / et. al. galaxy, and as such there are some seriously music-minded people behind the venture. As we mentioned in the Best of Miami issue, this is the rare, for-locals South Beach bar where your dollar will get you song selections from the likes of.

Tonight, though, it's worth heading over for the bar's weekly Wednesday human jukeboxes, especially if your chromosomes are of the xx variety. We at Crossfade don't usually endorse ladies' nights -- the concept usually screams watered-down fruit martinis and purse-clutching group dances to Beyonce.

The Kill Your Idol version is an exception to the cheese. Probably most importantly, women drink free all night. That's free, on the usual wells and beers, no catch, no buy-one requirements, no time cap. Got that? Behind the booze haze, too, are some killer tunes, courtesy of resident DJs Caroline and Desiree, as well as rotating female guests, who spin everything from vintage rock and roll to left-field electro to moody indie rock. The official party kicks off at 11 p.m.
name: Ladies Drink Free

description: All business people get 20% off food and booze any time of the day.
name: In the Biz

description:
You're at STK Steakhouse on the Beach grooving to the music. The waiter brings out your bone-in rib steak, done medium rare, just the way you like it. You sit down to dig in when you hear your favorite 80's tune and then you're on your feet again, dancing, the steak waiting for the music to slow down long enough for you to take a bite.

DJ Obscene, resident spinmeister at STK, says the customers' energy and response to his music that keeps him working those beloved '70s, '80s, and '90s dance tunes. But how does a 22-year old who wasn't even born when when Dead or Alive's "You Spin Me Round" hit the charts in 1985 know that this is what the crowd wants?

The self taught DJ, who started DJing at 14, says it's all about research, following his ear, and watching the crowd. "I look around to see who's singing along, dancing..." To him it's about exploring the music, taking diners on a journey while looking for cues from the crowd. "I've learned to love the '80's; they represent a great time in music when you had a little bit of everything; funk, soul, disco, rock, new wave and hip-hop." And people can relate, as the requests come in, he works them into the set. Happy diners beg for more.

But with diners dancing, what happens to the meal? We've all heard that music is often used as a marketing tool. A study done by Tufts University shows diners eat according to the beats of the music. With no music, participants ate at 3.9 bites per minute while with "spirited tunes," they sped up to an average of 5.1 bites per minute. The upbeat tempo helps turn tables faster, while a slower beat will keep guests around ordering more food.

Others believe that if a diner is eating fast he or she will finish before the brain has registered that the stomach is full, making a dessert order likely. Whichever it is, the owners of STK are not concerned. DJ Obscene's music keeps guests around and ordering all night long.

So what does he listen to when he eats dinner? "When I cook at home, smooth jazz." Really?? "The ambient music relaxes me and I focus on the food." And what does a 22 year old DJ love to eat? " I would have to say my mom's pork chops. We're Cuban and she really knows how to do them right"
name: DJ Obscene

description:
South Beach isn't shy about separating the haves from the have-nots. In fact, it relishes in its power to make things inaccessible to most. Take, for example, the Florida Room at the Delano, the Lenny Kravitz-designed space that transformed the hotel's basement into old Florida glamour with a modern twist. During Winter Music Conference alone, celebrities such as Jamie Foxx, David Guetta, Kevin Martin (Candlebox), Patrick Dahlheimer (Live), Jerry Harrison (Talking Heads), baseball star Roger Clemens, and tennis pro Andy Murray were all spotted at the jetsetter hot spot for the Delano Tuesday party. Described as "sexy nightlife" by promoter Scott Meszaros, the night sees plenty of beautiful and international clients.

The dinner/cocktail party starts at 9 p.m. on the hotel's main floor and casually moves downstairs to the Florida Room as the night progresses. South Beach tastemakers Tommy Pooch and Alan Roth host all of this high-end mayhem. There's no cover, but slow down there, buddy — this is the Beach after all. Bouncers let in only the best of the best, and there is a good chance you aren't it.
name: Delano Tuesdays

description: All locals get $3 beer and drinks.
name: Home Cooking

description:
In theory, revolution is sexy. You've read about the French insurgents and "liberté, égalité, fraternité" — not to mention their superior ideals, coed troops, and military-chic outfits — and it's all so gritty-glam. But then, in practice, the whole revolutionary-fervor thing invariably descends into shockingly inhuman blood and brutality. Just take a peek at the Frenchies' sequel: a little something called the Reign of Terror, featuring 16,594 official guillotine victims. Yikes.

That's why it's good to have people like party promoters Empire Events throwing mock radical get-downs such as Viva La Revolución at Louis this and every Tuesday. With DJs Rascal, Konflikt, Sub Zero, and Damaged Goods, it's the perfect place to sublimate our fantasies about antiestablishment action. So come clothed in the threads of aristocracy, pantaloons, the national cockade, or simple fatigues. The doors come down at 11 p.m., and there's no cover.
name: Viva La Revolución

description: Heineken for the guys and martinis for the girls.
name: Two-for-One

description: Ladies get complimentary admission, plus $1 cocktails and martinis while DJ Vertigo brings the beats.
name: Girls Night Out

description: Get half-price beer when you bring a pay stub.
name: In the Biz

description:
Miami is lucky to have a small legion of knockout DJs, the kind of head spinners who can actually floor a dance floor and then have the crowd screaming for more, more, more. But you can count on one hand the number of knockout DJs who are actual knockouts themselves. You know, those who have both chops and looks. And among the very few in that camp is a dame named Brooke G, a knockout in every sense of the word.

Now, before all you PC militants get your knickers in a twist, of course we know folks are supposed to be judged on their talents or their merits and not their looks. But even in this enlightened age, looks do count. Besides, when someone is both pleasing to the ears and easy on the eyes, why shouldn't we point it out?

This is the case with DJ Brooke G. Born and bred in the 305, this Magic City chick has been steadily besting the boys since the new millennium kicked in. She got her start in Beantown while a student at Boston University. Scoring a slot on the student station, WTBU, she eventually climbed from show host to music director.

During that spell, she also summered in L.A., boothing up everywhere from the Chateau Marmont to the Viper Room. Back on Miami's hallowed ground, Brooke G eventually spun a rave afterparty for the likes of Snoop and the Roots. She hasn't stopped spinning since.

Eventually, Brooke G took residence at the Shore Club, Privé, and Mansion and did much to make those spots hotter than they already had been. Now she rocks the hip-hop in the Red Room at Klutch, where owners Joe Delaney and SMAC have given her free reign to do what she does best. It's what she describes as a form of "live remixing," where her rock break-infused hip-hop becomes a sort of mashup pushed to a new limitlessness. Naturally, she does all of that with nothing but vinyl and Serato. But what else would you expect from someone with such respect for the power of song?

Among the tracks in heavy rotation are Rihanna's "Rude Boy" and Trina's "Million Dollar Girl." But Brooke G is not adverse to throwing back to the Beastie Boys' "Brass Monkey" or even, when the rockier side strikes her, Lynyrd Skynyrd's "What's Your Name?"

She says her dream night out would be when "the crowd ain't posing." And with Klutch's inimitable mix of louche and lascivious locals, she generally gets that opportunity every Friday night.
name: DJ Brooke G

description: The Bilt is now serving extra specialty drinks during brunch, including mango and peach bellinis, bloody marys, and bloody caesars as well as the old standbys, champagne and mimosas.
name: Booze at Brunch

description:
Tel Aviv has become something of a breeding ground for world class beat-keepers. Whether it comes from the psy-trance sweep of Infected Mushroom or the minimal tech-house of Miami transplant DJ Lee Or, Israel's second city is now a hotbed of beatitude.

And no wonder — OUT magazine called Tel Aviv "the gay capital of the Middle East," and it's been ranked by many as a global party town up there with both Barcelona and Miami. Add the fact that it's located on the Mediterranean coast, boasts the globe's largest concentration of modernist architecture, and doesn't shut down even when the sun comes up, and, well, you have a perfect confluence of geography, style, and action. That's just the kind of confluence that makes for dynamite nightclubbing.

Knowing all this, it makes a certain sense that now-local DJ Oren Nizri would call Tel Aviv his birthplace, and the place where he got his kick-start. He began breaking beats there in 2001 on the radio station the Voice of Tel Aviv with a show called In My House.

To continue reading about DJ Oren Nizri, click here to head to the music blog, Crossfade.
name: DJ Oren Nizri

description: Get $4 draft beer during any sports event.
name: Drinking Games

description: Everyone knows about the Delano’s Florida Room — the basement-like space transformed into a private playground for Miami’s A-list. But above ground, located in the lobby of the historic hotel, is the Rose Bar. You probably didn’t think you had any reason to visit, but now you do, thanks to an impromptu hipster dance party called Young, Fresh & New. It’s a Thursday-night weekend primer brought to you by South Beach scenesters Erica Fickling and Luke Dupont. From 9 p.m. to 2 a.m., DJ Ruen spins a fun mix of painfully cool classics and new Hype Machine-approved tracks. The winning combo has the hipsterati showing up in full force to play and party. And while the hotel’s bright lobby is a stark contrast to the Florida Room’s dim atmosphere, nobody seems to mind. There’s no cover, but your duds will be scrutinized at the door.
name: Young, Fresh & New

description:
The man has led a thousand lives and survived them all. Now 60 years old, Manno Charlemagne has been a singer-songwriter, political activist, and mayor of Port-au-Prince. Throughout the '80s and '90s, Haitian authorities incessantly harassed him for being a popular advocate of political change. He received death threats. He was abducted, jailed, and psychologically tortured by the national palace. Twice he was forced into exile from Haiti — first by dictator Baby Doc Duvalier in 1980 and then by Raoul Cédras's military junta from 1991 to 1994. And twice he returned.

Today, a decade after his short stint as mayor of Haiti's capital, Charlemagne lives in South Florida, where he has resumed his life as a twoubadou. Every Thursday at 8:30 p.m., the man and his band bring political chanson to Tap Tap as part of Monsieur Charlemagne's longtime residency at the Haitian landmark. And in honor of democratic ideals, there's never a cover charge.
name: Manno Charlemagne

description: With six days of round-the-clock events, you’ll have trouble staying awake or, God forbid, have to skip a few parties during White Party Week. What began in 1985 at Vizcaya as a massive celebration to raise money for HIV/AIDS research and awareness has turned into a global phenomenon drawing participants from all over the globe. Mova will host the White Heat Kick-Off party this Wednesday from 9 p.m. until 3 a.m. Admission is free, but do the world and your conscience a favor by making a donation at the door. If you’re in the mood for something pink, hit Bar 721 (721 Lincoln Ln., Miami Beach), where women will get down to raise awareness at Dolce: A Women’s Event. The bash begins this Wednesday at 10 p.m., and tickets cost $8 to $10. WPW will climax November 27 at Vizcaya (3251 S. Miami Ave., Miami), where the glamorously iconic White Party will offer samples from area restaurants, a silent auction, and the Viva Las Divas Casino Lounge. The party starts at 6:30 p.m.; tickets cost $150 for general admission and $250 for VIP. And don’t worry — you’ll have plenty of time to come down from your peak with other WPW 2010 highlights such as Muscle Beach at the 12th Street Beach and Noche Blanca at the Cameo Theater (1445 Washington Ave., Miami Beach), both November 29.
name: White Party Week

description: With giveaways like Dolphins tickets, Key West vacations, and other stuff.
name: Balloon Drop

description: Hard-core partiers like to hit four or five spots in one night. But a place that serves cocktails, dinner, and music is the 7-Eleven of luxe nightlife. The Bancroft Supper Club takes the convenience and vast selection of the Slurpee purveyor, omits the hot dogs, adds some style and panache, and brings SoBe its newest place to get bent, boogie, and eat amazing food. Part chic resto, part nightclub, and all housed within the decadence of the restored Bancroft Hotel building, the Bancroft Supper Club boasts a menu full of organic, natural foodstuffs — such as Wagyu beef tenderloin and homemade fettuccine — designed by chef Tim Andriola. After you’ve filled your belly with party fuel, let the DJ’s house, hip-hop, and dance beats transport you to the dance floor. Doors open every night for dinner at 5 p.m., and the cover-free party gets rolling at 10.
name: The Bancroft Supper Club

description: Get two bucks off all house lagers and wines, plus $5 mojitos, margaritas, and martinis during NFL games.
name: NFL Happy Hour

description: When hip-hop thugs G-Unit rap, "I move the keys, they call me the piano man," they're talking about transporting loads of happy powder, but when scene king Edison Farrow puts on a party called Piano Man, he's talking real keys, like the black-and-white ones at Crescendos Piano Bar. Each Wednesday, Farrow will bring a different ivory-tickler to woo you with the most harmonious sounds you've ever heard come from a granite bar. Yes, this is South Beach, so the piano is built into the bar. There's no cover charge, and the music will be center stage from 8 p.m. to 1 a.m.
name: Piano Man

description: Recoup with French toast, eggs Florentine, croissants, bloody marys, Bellinis, and tons of other tasty stuff.
name: Brunch

description:
Most people associate open-mike poetry nights with tie-dye, sneaky hits from Pyrex bowls, crusty flip-flops, and the stink of patchouli. But the Bohemia Room at Vlada Lounge is the “Boom Boom Pow” version of those hippie nightmares. Sure, there’ll be some political ranting, but it’ll likely be followed by Marvin Gaye’s “Mercy Mercy Me.” Resident DJ and house poet Anomaly chooses tracks according to the tone of the poet’s work onstage.

Host Ingrid B describes the Bohemia Room’s audience as sophisticated, college-educated, single urbanites in their mid-20s to mid-30s who are “grown and sexy.” The self-described “raunchy and hilarious” host offers the evening as something different from the regular weeknight. Every Wednesday evening, you can listen to poets pontificate about everything from sex to health care, down a few drinks, and meet some financially stable and intellectually stimulating hotties.
name: The Bohemia Room

description: Get Bud or Bud Lite for only $2.50.
name: Budweiser Blowout

description:
Long before South Beach became a hotbed of mediocrity, there lurked a contingent of sound and vision aficionados known as the Deep House Movement. DHM's core consisted of Omar Suardy, from New York, Stephen Flynn, from Ireland, and Edwin Adams, a Florida boy who had little in common with those in his Orlando hometown and was making a good go of things in the Magic City. The trio's goal was to create some of the most memorable evenings of music ever mustered, and it very often provided the time of your life.

After DHM had some stints up and down the strip, Tomas Ceddia of Aquabooty tapped the three to be resident DJs at his events. Ceddia and his business partner Joe Budious also had big ideas about how to make right the night. For the next decade, their teaming with DHM at venues ranging from the Marlin to Pawn Shop provided our town with the kind of fast action people still talk about.

Read the full story here.
name: Edwin Adams

description: Score pints for only $3.50.
name: Cheap Carlsberg

description: Bring your billiard balls to the table at Mickey's every second day of the week.
name: Free Pool

description: Reality shows make things look so easy, but in the real world, you don’t have the luxury of fancy editing and strategic cut-away shots that really make the magic happen. So when you’re boogying at the Wednesday-night Factory Milonga Tango Class and Party, look in the mirror and ask yourself: So you think you can dance? Each hump day at 9:30 p.m., join tango pros and wannabes as they attempt one of the sexiest dance forms on Earth (after the cabbage patch, anyway). The hourlong class takes you through the basics and urges you to inject the moves with your own personal style, but the milonga (exotic for “afterparty”), which begins at 10:30, is where you really get to show the hell off as live musicians and singers rock the Parafernalia Studio. Whether you take along a partner or keep it extra-mysterious and show up solo, be sure to bring your own cocktail so you really will think you can dance. The fun will run you ten bucks.
name: Factory Milonga Tango Class and Party

description: Get a free drink for wearing your Beach House tee. Or trade any other strip club shirt for a brand-new Beach House tee and earn yourself free cover and some complimentary booze.
name: Trade-In Tuesday

description: The PL0T and LINK crews have been busy this year hosting some of the top international techno talent at downtown venues like White Room, Electric Pickle and Space. Now they've embarked on an entirely new collaborative effort that aims to showcase Miami's own local talent in the intimate patio setting of La Folie on Washington Ave. every Wednesday night. South Beach can certainly use an injection of underground EDM sensibility, especially on a weeknight. Tonight's ON/OFF installment will feature minimal grooves by local DJ Hardline of Sobebeats, who made his 2008 WMC debut alongside Anja Schneider, Pan-Pot and Sebo K at the Mobilee Records Showcase and is also a regular at Space. He'll be joined by PL0T resident DJ Basti, another downtown regular who's recently played in support of artists like Alexi Delano, Wolf + Lamb, and Gaiser. With no cover, drink specials, and a tasteful soundtrack, ON/OFF at La Folie might just be the excuse you needed to party on a Wednesday night.
name: On/Off

description:
Miami may not have completely shed its reputation as a party mecca, even for its full-time residents. But with cats like DJ Manuvers coming up and taking over, we might one day also be known for our work ethic.

Of course, you might expect some fast action from one whose name is both a noun and a verb conjugation. (His real name is similarly double-sided; he was born Francisco de Pablo in Santiago, Chile, but his pals just call him "Pancho.") His DJ name springs from a friend, and the spelling comes from hip-hop's phonetic tradition. Its meaning, however — as in one who makes the moves — is all him.

Those moves have included boothing up everywhere from Soho Lounge and Opium Hard Rock to Barcelona's Sonar Festival, where Manuvers spun alongside everyone from Carl Cox to 2 Many DJs. These days, those moves run another gamut, from Electric Pickle's Champion Sound Wednesday weekly party to Purdy Lounge's Chocolate Sundays, with News Lounge in the middle.

Manuvers' moves also included helping to helm the now-defunct Counterflow Recordings, which in its five-year existence gave us some 60 to 70 releases, the majority of them on beloved vinyl.

Now he's all about a new project, Hometeam Music, which will join forces with DJ Induce's Wondersound Recordings for this summer's much-anticipated album, The Wonderful World of Induce.
